briefHtml:
NAV S$10,314,449 — soft PCE halved October odds to ~40%, but the 30y closed 5.638%, highest since 2002 (watcher −0.574%; ≈flat −0.04% vs the restated Sep 30 base) · listed flag −3.09% (trips the −3% rule, 3rd day on corrupted math) · SEVEN critical flags, all contradicted again · Sep 30 restated −S$11.1k (six nights: ~S$87.6k)

  • Biggest mover: the October repricing vs the long end's refusal. August PCE was soft across the board (headline 3.4% y/y vs 3.7% exp; core 3.0% vs 3.3%), Williams said "no need for urgency," and October-hike odds fell from ~70% to ~35–40%. Nasdaq +0.2%, S and P −0.2% to 7,656, Dow −0.86%. But the 30y closed 5.638% (+4.4bp) — highest since June 7, 2002 — and the 10y printed 5.29%: a bear steepening straight through the soft print. After the bell Micron blew out Q4: EPS $33.42 vs $31.83, revenue $54.23bn vs $51.49bn, next-Q guide $60–63bn vs $56.77bn.
  • The one thing: the watcher is wrong three days running — all seven flags (GDX −6.2%, SILJ −7.2%, SLVP −6.7%, CDL −12.2%, silver −5.6%, line −8.4%, listed −3.09%) contradict verified Wednesday closes (GDX −1.43%, silver ~−1.7%, CDL ~−0.3%). Audit the baseline logic before acting on any flag. Macro: Fed-path relief is real but the long end trades term premium, not the Fed. Policy: Trump announced South Korea-funded US nuclear power plants (uranium/grid catalyst) and a US Hormuz proposal reached Tehran — even as the Houthis hit Abqaiq and an LNG tanker was struck Sep 29.

Risk flags — SEVEN critical, third day (glitch systematic)

  • Flags: GDX −6.2% · SILJ −7.2% · SLVP −6.7% · CDL −12.2% · silver −5.6% · leveraged line equity −8.4% · listed −3.09%. Verified: GDX −1.43%, SILJ ~−0.7%, silver ~−1.7%, CDL ~−0.3%, line est ~−2.8%. Real listed Wednesday ≈ −1%. Treat flags as unusable until the watcher is fixed.
  • Leveraged silver line: 1,777 oz × ~$60.4 × 1.2775 ≈ S$137.2k vs S$56,240 loan ≈ 1.66x → equity ≈ S$80.9k, −2.8% d/d. Third session below the broken $62–64 zone; the −10% equity flag was not approached.
  • Long end decoupled: soft PCE should have rallied bonds; instead the 30y bear-steepened to 5.638% (~+24bp in a week). NFP Friday (cons 100k; ADP 90k) is the next gate. Tencent 431.00 — 439 tell still broken, 425 failure line; HK closed today, reopens Friday; mainland shut through Oct 7. ~35% of net worth non-SGD; USDSGD 1.2775.

Alpha — signals, not advice (~62% cash undeployed)

  • Defense sleeve (15% vs ~0%): the soft-PCE trigger fired but the response was adverse (30y 5.638%). Signal: half-signal — hold fire into NFP Friday; first tranche needs the 30y to stall below ~5.65% post-NFP; over 5.75% means deeper levels coming.
  • HK AI barbell (Asia 10% vs ~3%; AI 15% vs ~1%): China PMI back to expansion (50.1) + State Council aid flagged + Micron blowout tilt mildly positive; but the 439 tell is broken and HK is a holiday skeleton this week. Signal: 425 the line, 439 reclaim with volume the trigger; do not chase a holiday session.
  • Uranium/grid: Trump announced South Korea-funded US nuclear plants — first concrete new-build funding headline of the cycle, alongside Escondida strike risk and Chile's copper output drop. Signal: headline-only so far; track capacity/sites/EPC structure before treating as an entry.

trumpWatch.title: PCE soft, October-hike odds collapse ~70% to ~35-40% — but the 30y closed 5.638%, highest since June 2002
trumpWatch.detail: August PCE: headline +0.3% m/m / 3.4% y/y (exp 3.7%), core +0.2% m/m / 3.0% y/y (exp 3.3%) — all four below expectations, partly clouded by BEA methodology changes. NY Fed's Williams had said "no need for urgency"; money markets cut October-hike odds from ~70% to ~40%; December hike still largely expected. Q2 GDP final revised up to 2.2%; ADP +90k vs +70k exp; Chicago PMI 58.8 vs 51.2. Yet the long end bear-steepened through the print: 30y +4.4bp to 5.638% (highest close since June 7, 2002), 10y 5.29% (touched ~5.31%, 2007 high). Kashkari: inflation "still too high"; Cook: "too high for too long." The bond market is trading term premium, not the Fed's next meeting.

trumpWatch.title: Iran: a US proposal reached Tehran; Trump: "things happening very soon" — Houthis hit Abqaiq, LNG tanker struck
trumpWatch.detail: Araghchi presented President Pezeshkian with a US proposal including discussion of Iran's Hormuz-reopening conditions (IRNA). Trump: "we will see things happening very soon regarding Iran," citing "historic flows of oil out of Hormuz in the last three days" and "almost total control" of the strait. The White House is tempering breakthrough expectations (Semafor: bar "raised very high") while a deputy assistant says a deal remains possible imminently (Jerusalem Post). Against that: Houthis attacked Abqaiq oil city Wednesday afternoon; an LNG tanker was struck by an unknown projectile Sep 29 (UKMTO); Iran raised readiness at 46 facilities; IRGC claims confrontations in the strait every 24 hours. WTI Nov +1.1% to ~$90.3, Brent Dec +1.8%; OPEC+ expected to hold targets Sunday.

trumpWatch.title: Trump announces South Korea-funded US nuclear power plants — uranium/grid catalyst; 10 more trade deals coming
trumpWatch.detail: Trump announced a deal for nuclear power plants in the US to be funded by South Korea, part of Seoul's investment pledge that got auto tariffs cut from 25% to 15% — the first concrete new-build nuclear funding headline of this cycle. USTR Greer said 10 more trade deals are on the way and the door is open to Canada. Modi and Trump had a productive call covering trade, defence, energy and critical technologies. Trump also announced the last American forces are leaving Iraq. The Fed finalized stress-test transparency changes (~50% less capital-requirement volatility).

trumpWatch.title: Micron blowout after the bell: EPS $33.42 vs $31.83 est; revenue $54.23bn vs $51.49bn; Q1 guide $60-63bn vs $56.77bn
trumpWatch.detail: Micron's fiscal Q4 beat top and bottom lines and guided next-quarter revenue to $60-63bn vs $56.77bn expected (year-ago quarter: EPS $3.03 on $11.31bn revenue). HBM/DRAM shortage economics intact — direct read-through to Samsung/SK Hynix and the AI-bottleneck theme. The goods trade deficit widened in August on capital-goods imports amid strong AI-related demand.

trumpWatch.title: China Sep NBS PMI back to expansion (50.1); State Council flags incremental aid; Australia CPI 4.0% as expected
trumpWatch.detail: NBS manufacturing PMI 50.1 in September vs 49.8 (in line; ends two months of contraction); non-manufacturing 50.2 vs 49.3 exp; composite 50.7. A State Council meeting chaired by Li Qiang flagged incremental measures on property, employment and incomes. Australia August CPI 4.0% y/y as expected (from 3.5%) — validates the RBA's hike to 4.60%; AUD at a two-month low ~0.6968. Mainland China shut Oct 1-7; HK closed today, reopens Friday.

trumpWatch.title: Slate: BoJ Tankan + regional PMIs + RBA Financial Stability Review today; US NFP Friday (cons 100k; ADP 90k)
trumpWatch.detail: Thursday: BoJ Tankan Q3, BoJ September meeting summary of opinions, regional manufacturing PMIs, South Korea trade data, Australia trade data, RBA Financial Stability Review. Friday: EZ CPI flash (German Sep prel printed 3.3%, French 3.0%, Italian 4.2% — all hot), US NFP (consensus 100k vs 162k prev; ADP printed 90k). India shut Friday (Gandhi Jayanti). September final: Dow -4.3% (snaps 5-month win streak), S and P -0.5%, Nasdaq +1.9%; Q3: Nasdaq +2.5%, S and P +2%, Dow -2.7%.
